A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dynamic Focus Decoding (DFD) research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched reliably despite additions and page reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations across seven datasets, including decoding comparisons, ablations, computational measurements and dynamic focus training results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds FactScore evaluations and results for additional decoding settings.

M1.justification: The layer-wise KL aggregation, vocabulary constraint, three temperature transformations, decoding procedure and focused training loss remain unchanged. Section 3.2 expands their explanation without changing the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TruthfulQA, StrategyQA, CommonGen, WikiText-103, Wikinews, Vicuna QA and HalluDial for the same tasks. The additional sampling configurations change experimental settings, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Within the robustness comparison in Section 5.3 and Figure 4, v2 adds top-k, nucleus and locally typical sampling alongside temperature sampling, each compared with its DFD extension. Main benchmark and DoLa comparisons retain their comparator sets. Newly cited contrastive-search methods are not evaluated.

E3.justification: FactScore supplements MAUVE for document continuation. Section 5.3 adds sweeps over k={10,50,100}, p={0.9,0.95,0.98} and tau={0.9,0.95,0.98}, retaining the temperature sweep. Previously stated data sampling, default configurations and generation lengths remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The decoding sensitivity analysis expands from three temperature settings to parameter sweeps for four sampling algorithms. Layer aggregation, transformation, model-scale, DoLa integration, efficiency, training and case-study analyses retain their existing evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions state that responses are generated three times and results averaged. Neither adds seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 4 and 14 add FactScore results: for example, v2 reports WikiText-103 scores of 42.83 for temperature sampling and 45.09 with DFD. Figure 4 adds findings at non-default k, p and tau settings. Existing numerical results are retained; Distinct-2 values omitted from main Table 4 remain in appendix Table 14.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14, including the KL–PMI reasoning and knowledge-awareness definition, retain their mathematical content. Changes to equation formatting and explanatory prose introduce no new assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: DFD improves factuality and diversity through adaptive decoding focus, requires no additional data or models for inference, and incurs minimal computational overhead.

C2.justification: Interpretations of layer-wise knowledge, the factuality–diversity balance and dynamic focus training remain substantively unchanged. Expanded knowledge-awareness and chatbot explanations restate existing interpretations. The limitations concerning inaccurate, biased or outdated parametric knowledge are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement with a repository address and Table 21 documenting the TruthfulQA instruction and demonstration prompt. These improve access and implementation information; the PDFs do not establish that the prompt itself changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Min et al. (2023) for FactScore and a related-work sentence citing Su et al. (2022), Su and Collier (2023), and Arias et al. (2024) on contrastive approaches to coherence and diversity. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized revisions expand Section 3.2 and the chatbot discussion and rewrite the robustness paragraph. v2 also adds author contact information and acknowledgments, standardizes Top-k terminology and removes some appendix cross-references. Most prose and the section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 improves contrast by using white labels in dark cells. Figure 4 expands from one panel to four and is relocated. Tables 4 and 14 accommodate FactScore, and Table 21 adds the prompt template. The overall document layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's MAUVE-only document-continuation assessment, v2 adds FactScore evidence relevant to factual precision. Broader sampling-parameter checks and prompt/code disclosures strengthen empirical support and reproducibility information. These are useful incremental improvements, although the new FactScore evaluation receives little implementation detail.
